title: `wasmJs` artifact missing from Maven Central — `Unresolved reference 'ismoy'` when compiling for wasmJs target
body_excerpt: When using `imagepickerkmp` in a Kotlin Multiplatform project that includes a `wasmJs` target, compilation fails with `Unresolved reference 'ismoy'` errors for all classes from the library (`rememberImagePickerKMP`, `ImagePickerKMPConfig`, `GalleryConfig`, `ImagePickerResult`, `PhotoResult`). The library is declared in `commonMain.dependencies`, which works correctly for Android, iOS, and Desktop targets. However, the `wasmJs` target fails to compile because the `imagepickerkmp-wasm-js` artifact does not appear to be published to Maven Central. The README and release notes (including 1.0.35) advertise WASM support, but only the following artifacts are available on Maven Central: - `imagepickerkmp-android` - `imagepickerkmp-iosarm64` - `imagepickerkmp-iossimulatorarm64` - `imagepickerkmp-js` - `imagepickerkmp-jvm` There is no `imagepickerkmp-wasm-js` artifact published. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a KMP project with `wasmJs { browser(); binaries.executable() }` target 2. Add `implementation("io.github.ismoy:imagepickerkmp:1.0.41")` to `commonMain.dependencies` 3. Use any class from the library (e.g. `rememberImagePickerKMP`) 4. Run `./gradlew :composeApp:wasmJsBrowserDistribution` ## Error ``` e: Unresolved reference 'ismoy'. e: Unresolved reference 'rememberImagePickerKMP'. e: Unresolved reference 'ImagePickerKMPConfig'. e: Unresolved reference 'GalleryConfig'. e: Unresolved reference 'ImagePickerResult'. e: Unresolved reference 'PhotoResult'. ``` ## Environment - Library version: `1.0.41` - Kotlin: `2.3.20` - Compose Multiplatform: latest - Targets: Android, iOS, wasmJs ## Expected Behavior The `imagepickerkmp-wasm-js` artifact is published to Maven Central so that `wasmJs` target can resolve the library from `commonMain`. ## Workaround Currently the only workaround is to move all usages of the library out of `commonMain` into platform-specific source sets using `expect`/`actual`, with a stub implementation for `wasmJsMain`.

title: Linux V8-mode libraries are not linked against libm — `undefined symbol: exp2` on OpenJ9
body_excerpt: ## Summary Since v5.0.0, `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64.v.*.so` is built without a link to `libm`. It leaves 12 math symbols undefined (`exp2`, `log2`, `pow`, `nan`, `nearbyint`, among others) and relies on the host process to already provide them. That assumption holds on HotSpot, whose `libjvm.so` links `libm.so.6` and is loaded into the global symbol scope, so the undefined symbols quietly bind. It does not hold on Eclipse OpenJ9 / IBM Semeru: their `libjvm.so` links only `libdl`, `libpthread` and `libc`, so nothing fills the gap and the process aborts on the first call. Because the dynamic linker resolves these lazily, the failure surfaces only when one of those symbols is first called, which in practice is V8 teardown at JVM shutdown: ``` java: symbol lookup error: /tmp/javet/2552/libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64.v.5.0.3.so: undefined symbol: exp2 ``` The symbols were missing the whole time — they were simply never called before that point. ## Affected versions v5.0.0 through at least v5.0.3, V8 mode, Linux. Node mode is not affected. | Artifact | `NEEDED` | Unresolved math symbols | |---|---|---| | `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64` 4.1.7 | `libm.so.6`, `libc.so.6` | 0 | | `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64` 5.0.0 | `librt.so.1`, `libc.so.6` | 12 | | `libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64` 5.0.3 | `librt.so.1`, `libc.so.6` | 12 | `linux-arm64` was not measured, but it is produced by the same CMake branch and is expected to be affected identically. Worth confirming as part of the fix. ## Environment - JVM: Eclipse OpenJ9 / IBM Semeru 21 and 25 — both affected - HotSpot: not affected (masks the problem rather than avoiding it) - OS: not a factor. `ldd -r` gives identical results on glibc 2.40 and on Ubuntu Noble, and the error reproduces on both. glibc-based distributions only; musl was not tested. ## Reproduction ```bash # 1. Show the unresolved symbols in the shipped artifact ldd -r libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64.v.5.0.3.so # -> 12 "undefined symbol: ..." lines for math functions readelf -d libjavet-v8-linux-x86_64.v.5.0.3.so | grep NEEDED # -> librt.so.1, libc.so.6 ... no libm.so.6 # 2. Trigger it: run any V8-mode script on OpenJ9/Semeru and let the JVM exit. # The error appears during V8 teardown. # 3. Confirm the cause by supplying libm externally LD_PRELOAD=/lib64/libm.so.6 java -jar app.jar # -> 12 unresolved symbols become 0, error gone ``` ## Root cause `cpp/cmake/platforms/Linux.cmake:53-64` — the `if(DEFINED V8_DIR)` branch links with `-nostdlib++` and passes the libc++ / libc++abi archives explicitly: ```cmake set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -nostdinc++ -fno-exceptions ... ") target_link_libraries(Javet PUBLIC -Wl,-Bstatic -latomic -Wl,-Bdynamic -Wl,--compress-sections=.text=none -Wl,--whole-archive ${importLibraries} -Wl,--no-whole-archive ${LIBCXX_STATIC} ${LIBCXXABI_STATIC} debug "-lrt" -static-libgcc -nostdlib++ optimized "-lrt" "${libgcc}") ``` Taking the C++ runtime out of the compiler driver's hands also took the implicit `-lm` with it, and nothing adds it back. Since undefined symbols are permitted in a shared object by default, the link succeeds silently. This traces to commit `4c649003` "Switch to clang for V8 mode on Linux" (#524), which moved the Linux V8 build from GCC with `-static-libstdc++` to clang with libc++. Nothing in that change was about math, which is why it went unnoticed. The Node.js branch at `cpp/cmake/platforms/Linux.cmake:80-89` still uses `-static-libstdc++`, so the driver still contributes its standard library group and `-lm` survives. That is consistent with Node-mode artifacts being unaffected. Note: the precise driver-level reason `-lm` disappears is inferred from the artifact diff plus the GCC→clang switch. A `clang++ -###` dump of both link lines would pin it down exactly, but it does not change the fix. ## Proposed fix Add `-lm` to both targets in the V8-mode branch of `cpp/cmake/platforms/Linux.cmake`, restoring the pre-5.0.0 `NEEDED: libm.so.6`: ```cmake target_link_libraries(Javet PUBLIC ... debug "-lrt" "-lm" -static-libgcc -nostdlib++ optimized "-lrt" "-lm" "${libgcc}") target_link_libraries(JavetStatic PUBLIC ... debug "-lrt" "-lm" -static-libgcc -nostdlib++ optimized "-lrt" "-lm" "${libgcc}") ``` Static linkage (`-Wl,-Bstatic -lm -Wl,-Bdynamic`) would also resolve the symbols, but static libm against a dynamic glibc is not a supported glibc configuration — the two share internal state — so dynamic `-lm` is the safer route. ### Suggested guard against regressions The failure mode here is that a missing link dependency produces a library that loads fine and only fails much later, under one specific JVM. A post-build check would catch the whole class of problem: ```bash ldd -r "$LIB" 2>&1 | grep "undefined symbol" && exit 1 ``` Running that in CI for each Linux artifact turns a silent packaging defect into a build failure. ## Workaround for users Preload the system libm so the symbols are in the global scope before Javet loads, which is what HotSpot does implicitly: ```bash export LD_PRELOAD=/lib64/libm.so.6 # SLE, RHEL export LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6 # Debian, Ubuntu ``` Verified to take the 12 unresolved symbols to 0. Staying on HotSpot also avoids the symptom, but leaves the underlying packaging defect in place.

title: [Bug] API compatibility crashes on Android 8.1 Tablet: Widget Sheet (API 28) and App Popup Split Screen (API 29)
body_excerpt: ### Describe the bug On an Android 8.1 (API 27) tablet, Lawnchair crashes when triggering two core features from specific menus, while both features work when triggered via alternative system paths. Both crashes are caused by the launcher attempting to access newer Android APIs that do not exist on API 27: 1. **Widget Picker Crash:** Long-pressing an empty space on the home screen and tapping "Widgets" causes an immediate crash (`NoSuchMethodError: setAccessibilityPaneTitle`, an API 28+ method). * *Alternative path that works:* Long-pressing an app icon and picking its widget from the popup menu works completely fine without crashing. 2. **Split Screen Crash:** Long-pressing an app icon and selecting "Split screen" from the popup menu causes a crash (`NoClassDefFoundError: android.app.TaskInfo`, an API 29+ class). * *Alternative path that works:* Entering split-screen directly from the system Recent Apps / Overview screen works without issue. ### Steps to reproduce **Case A: Widget Picker Crash** 1. Long-press an empty space on the home screen. 2. Tap on "Widgets". 3. Launcher crashes immediately. *(Counter-test: Long-pressing an app icon > selecting widgets works).* **Case B: Split Screen Crash** 1. Long-press any app icon on the home screen or app drawer. 2. Tap on "Split screen" from the popup menu. 3. Launcher crashes immediately. *(Counter-test: Splitting screens via the system Overview / Recents view works).* ### Expected behavior 1. title: Incorrect Current/Wattage Parsing and Unread Cycle Counts on Samsung Galaxy A15 5G (MediaTek Dimensity 6100+)
body_excerpt: On the Samsung Galaxy A15 5G running One UI, Amply reads charging current as 0W (or 1mA), and charge cycles are not displayed. Inspection via dumpsys battery reveals that the device's MediaTek power management driver outputs current now directly as a 3-digit milliamp integer (441) rather than standard microamps muA, e.g., 441000). Because the app assumes microamps, dividing 441 by 1,000,000 results in approx 0.0004A, which rounds down to 0W. Additionally, total cycle usage is logged under Samsung's custom MediaTek key mSavedBatteryUsage: [54327] (representing 543.27\% accumulated usage / ~543 cycles) instead of the standard Android HAL cycle_count integer, causing cycle reporting to fail. Please add MediaTek unit scaling (mA vs muA) and mSavedBatteryUsage fallback parsing for this device model.

title: Crash: recording waveform races on AudioCaptureManager energy history
body_excerpt: ## Root cause Physical Pixel gate on integrated `develop` commit `6138ef5` reproduced a main-thread crash while recording. `AudioCaptureManager.energyHistory` is an unsynchronized `ArrayDeque`: the capture coroutine mutates it while the timer/main path calls `getEnergyHistory().toList()`. A racing snapshot can expose a transient null backing-array slot, which Kotlin then unboxes in `WaveformBars` and crashes. ## Physical evidence - Pixel 4 (`flame`), Android 15/API 35, ARM64, serial `99071FFAZ00EBN` - exact APK SHA-256: `83be3a08102df9c233493517b6ce9497a3145824ebbee905c4c475b1a3324a17` - microphone capture and foreground service started correctly - crash: `java.lang.NullPointerException` at `WaveformBars.kt:64`, observed while the capture coroutine was updating waveform history - no audio or transcript retained ## Acceptance criteria - Synchronize all reads and writes of the rolling energy history without changing waveform behavior. - Add a deterministic concurrent read/write regression test that fails on the old implementation. - Run targeted tests, all JVM tests, lint, and assemble. - Prove the regression test bites via sabotage/revert. - Independent fresh-context review and exact-head Pixel recording smoke with no crash/ANR. ## Scope/risk Small thread-safety repair; no persisted-state/API/migration changes. Rollback is a single commit. Tracked by #33.

[Bug] Systematic Cursor Leaks in Adapters (FavoriteAdapter & TagsAdapter) during Filter Cancellation
body_excerpt: ### Checklist - [x] I have looked at the common issues and ways to fix them in the [wiki](https://github.com/maxwai/NClientV3/wiki) - [x] I have searched the existing issues for the same bug - [x] I have attached the log file as an attachment to this issue ### Describe the bug ## Summary During a review of the application's resource management, we identified a systematic `Cursor` leak in the Android `Filter` implementations within `FavoriteAdapter` and `TagsAdapter`. When a user types rapidly in the search fields, the Android `Filter` framework cancels ongoing background filtering tasks to start new ones. According to Android documentation, when a task is cancelled, `publishResults` is **never invoked**. Because the current implementations pass open `Cursor` objects directly into `FilterResults.values`, these cursors are never closed upon cancellation, leading to severe resource leaks. ## Affected Components & Code Analysis ### 1. `FavoriteAdapter.java` (Lines 129–148) In `performFiltering`, a `Cursor` is created via `Queries.FavoriteTable.getAllFavoriteGalleriesCursor()` and assigned to `results.values`. The cursor is only closed inside `publishResults` -> `updateCursor()`. If cancelled, the cursor is lost and leaked. ### 2. `TagsAdapter.java` Similarly, `performFiltering` assigns `Queries.TagTable.getFilterCursor(...)` to `results.values` without lifecycle safeguards. Furthermore, in `publishResults`, there is an early return (`if (results.count == -1) return;`) that skips closing the previously passed `Cursor`, creating an additional leak path. ## Impact - **Resource Exhaustion:** Each unclosed `Cursor` holds references to file descriptors and database connection handles. - **Rapid Accumulation:** Fast typing in search fields triggers multiple cancelled filters, quickly exhausting the per‑process cursor limit (typically 1024). - **Stability Issues:** This leads to `CursorWindowAllocationException`, `IOException: Too many open files`, or `OutOfMemoryError`, eventually crashing the app. - **Severity:** High. ## Code Analysis **File:** `NClientV3/app/src/main/java/com/maxwai/nclientv3/adapters/FavoriteAdapter.java` **Lines 129–148 (inside `getFilter()` anonymous `Filter`):** ```java @Override protected FilterResults performFiltering(CharSequence constraint) { constraint = constraint.toString().toLowerCase(Locale.US); if ((!force && lastQuery.equals(constraint))) return null; LogUtility.d("FILTERING"); setRefresh(true); FilterResults results = new FilterResults(); lastQuery = constraint.toString(); LogUtility.d(lastQuery + "LASTQUERY"); force = false; // ❌ LEAK POINT: Cursor created here Cursor c = Queries.FavoriteTable.getAllFavoriteGalleriesCursor( lastQuery, sortByTitle, perPage, (activity.getActualPage() - 1) * perPage); results.count = c.getCount(); results.values = c; // ❌ Cursor escapes; if filter cancelled, never closed LogUtility.d("FILTERING3"); LogUtility.d(results.count + ";" + results.values); setRefresh(false); return results; } ``` The [Android Filter documentation](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/widget/Filter) states that when a new filter request is issued before the previous one finishes, the framework cancels the earlier operation and **does not** invoke `publishResults`. In the current code: - `performFiltering()` returns the open `Cursor` inside `FilterResults.values`. - `publishResults()` (line 145) passes the cursor to `updateCursor()`, which is the only place where the cursor is eventually closed. - When cancellation occurs, `publishResults()` is never called, so the cursor from the cancelled task remains open indefinitely. ## Suggested Fix Extract the required data from the `Cursor` **inside** `performFiltering()` and close it immediately. Return a lightweight, non‑resource‑holding object (e.g. `List<Gallery>`) through `FilterResults.values`. This guarantees the cursor is always closed, regardless of whether the filter completes or is cancelled. **Modified `performFiltering()`:** ```java @Override protected FilterResults performFiltering(CharSequence constraint) { constraint = constraint.toString().toLowerCase(Locale.US); if (!force && lastQuery.equals(constraint)) return null; LogUtility.d("FILTERING"); setRefresh(true); FilterResults results = new FilterResults(); lastQuery = constraint.toString(); LogUtility.d(lastQuery + "LASTQUERY"); force = false; Cursor c = null; try { c = Queries.FavoriteTable.getAllFavoriteGalleriesCursor( lastQuery, sortByTitle, perPage, (activity.getActualPage() - 1) * perPage); List<Gallery> galleryList = new ArrayList<>(c.getCount()); while (c.moveToNext()) { galleryList.add(Queries.GalleryTable.cursorToGallery(activity, c)); } results.count = galleryList.size(); results.values = galleryList; // ✅ Return List, not Cursor LogUtility.d("FILTERING3"); LogUtility.d(results.count + ";" + results.values); } finally { if (c != null) { c.close(); // ✅ Always closed, even on cancellation } } setRefresh(false); return results; } ``` Correspondingly adjust `publishResults()` to work with the `List<Gallery>` instead of a `Cursor`. For example: ```java @Override protected void publishResults(CharSequence constraint, FilterResults results) { if (results == null) return; setRefresh(true); final int oldSize = getItemCount(); @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") List<Gallery> newGalleries = (List<Gallery>) results.values; final int newSize = newGalleries.size(); updateGalleries(newGalleries); // New helper that replaces updateCursor(Cursor) if (oldSize > newSize) notifyItemRangeRemoved(newSize, oldSize - newSize); else notifyItemRangeInserted(oldSize, newSize - oldSize); notifyItemRangeChanged(0, Math.min(newSize, oldSize)); setRefresh(false); } ``` And introduce a small helper to manage the adapter data without holding a `Cursor`: ```java private void updateGalleries(@Nullable List<Gallery> newGalleries) { if (newGalleries == null || newGalleries.isEmpty()) { galleries = new Gallery[0]; } else { galleries = newGalleries.toArray(new Gallery[0]); } if (cursor != null) cursor.close(); cursor = null; statuses.clear(); } ``` This approach decouples the adapter from cursor lifecycle management, ensures resources are released immediately, and makes the code more robust against filter cancellations. ### Steps To Reproduce This issue was identified through static code analysis, and has been verified manually. ### Expected behavior See "Impact". ### Screenshots _No response_ ### Android Version 14 ### App Version main-branch ### Additional context Context & Acknowledgement This issue was identified during academic research on Java resource management and API invocation hazards in Android applications. We have manually reviewed this finding to ensure its validity. Thank you for maintaining NClientV3! We hope this report helps.

Otherwise consider posting your into() or clear() calls to the main thread using a Handler instead. at com.bumptech.glide.request.SingleRequest.assertNotCallingCallbacks(SingleRequest.java:289) at com.bumptech.glide.request.SingleRequest.clear(SingleRequest.java:309) at com.bumptech.glide.manager.RequestTracker.clearAndRemove(RequestTracker.java:72) at com.bumptech.glide.RequestManager.untrack(RequestManager.java:660) at com.bumptech.glide.RequestManager.untrackOrDelegate(RequestManager.java:628) at com.bumptech.glide.RequestManager.clear(RequestManager.java:624) at io.getstream.avatarview.glide.AvatarBitmapLoader$loadBitmaps$1$2.invoke(AvatarBitmapLoader.kt:91) at io.getstream.avatarview.glide.AvatarBitmapLoader$loadBitmaps$1$2.invoke(AvatarBitmapLoader.kt:90) ``` The error refers to this code ``` awaitClose { requestManager.clear(avatarViewTarget) } ``` Since Glide loads images on the main thread, it seems that we can fix this problem by adding `launch(Dispatchers.Main)` to ``` launch() { val avatarResults: ArrayList<AvatarResult> = arrayListOf() val avatarResultFlow = AvatarBitmapLoader.loadBitmaps( requestManager = Glide.with(this@collectAndCombineBitmaps), data = data, errorPlaceholder = errorPlaceholder ) ``` But not sure if that would be the right decision.

title: PDF417 Incorrect dimension error?
body_excerpt: If I use: ```java protected BufferedImage generatePDF417Image(final String barcodeText, final int width, final Integer heightRequested) throws WriterException { final Writer barcodeWriter = new PDF417Writer(); final int height = heightRequested == null ? width / 4 : heightRequested; final Map<EncodeHintType, ?> hints = Map.of(EncodeHintType.MARGIN, 0, EncodeHintType.PDF417_DIMENSIONS, new Dimensions(1, 30, 7, 7)); final BitMatrix bitMatrix = barcodeWriter.encode(barcodeText, BarcodeFormat.PDF_417, width, height, hints); return MatrixToImageWriter.toBufferedImage(bitMatrix); } ``` and call it with ```java generatePDF417Image("0000000001000000022200000003330444400888888881010101010", 371, null); ``` I hit the ```java throw new WriterException("Unable to fit message in columns"); ``` in the PDF417.class (line 735 at time of viewing) If I use EncodeHintType.PDF417_DIMENSIONS, new Dimensions(5, 30, 7, 7) it works, but this has the same maxCols and has only increased the minCols value. I think this is due to ```java int rows = calculateNumberOfRows(sourceCodeWords, errorCorrectionCodeWords, minCols); ``` using the minCols value where I think it should use the cols calculated before breaking in the above loop. I think the following code would work as desired: ```java private int[] determineDimensions(int sourceCodeWords, int errorCorrectionCodeWords) throws WriterException { float ratio = 0.0f; int[] dimension = null; int currentCols = minCols; for (int cols = minCols; cols <= maxCols; cols++) { currentCols = cols; int rows = calculateNumberOfRows(sourceCodeWords, errorCorrectionCodeWords, cols); if (rows < minRows) { break; } if (rows > maxRows) { continue; } float newRatio = ((float) (17 * cols + 69) * DEFAULT_MODULE_WIDTH) / (rows * HEIGHT); // ignore if previous ratio is closer to preferred ratio if (dimension != null && Math.abs(newRatio - PREFERRED_RATIO) > Math.abs(ratio - PREFERRED_RATIO)) { continue; } ratio = newRatio; dimension = new int[] {cols, rows}; } // Handle case when min values were larger than necessary if (dimension == null) { int rows = calculateNumberOfRows(sourceCodeWords, errorCorrectionCodeWords, currentCols); if (rows < minRows) { dimension = new int[]{minCols, minRows}; } } if (dimension == null) { throw new WriterException("Unable to fit message in columns"); } return dimension; } ```

title: Mac OS fullscreen mode does not cover the Mac Dock completely, unless window is setResizable(false)
body_excerpt: #### Issue details I've received a report from players that my game, when run in fullscreen mode on Mac OS, "appears" to be fullscreen, but the Apple Dock at the bottom of the screen is still interactable. (i.e. the player can click where the dock is, and they'll be taken out of the game.) After doing a bunch of hacking, it seems a workaround is by setting `resizable` on the window to `false`. This results in the window on Mac to be a better, more behaved fullscreen. I'm not sure if this is intended behaviour or not? _Please provide the details of your issue_ #### Reproduction steps/code I'm setting fullscreen mode like so: ```java DisplayMode displayMode = getFirstDisplayModeWithTheSameMonitorDimensionsAs(Gdx.graphics.getMonitor()); Gdx.graphics.setFullscreenMode(displayMode); ``` But this seems to work as desired: ```java DisplayMode displayMode = getFirstDisplayModeWithTheSameMonitorDimensionsAs(Gdx.graphics.getMonitor()); Gdx.graphics.setResizable(false); // important for Mac to make sure the fullscreen is actually fullscreen!? Gdx.graphics.setFullscreenMode(displayMode); ``` #### Version of libGDX and/or relevant dependencies * LibGDX 1.12.0 * lwjgl 3.3.3 * Mac OS 10.15.7 #### Please select the affected platforms - [ ] Android - [ ] iOS - [ ] HTML/GWT - [ ] Windows - [ ] Linux - [x] macOS
